note: Mode-tagged should-trigger phrasings and near-miss negatives that must route elsewhere. Used by the description trigger check across all five modes. Operate fires on work that crosses departments; one department's own work, asked alone, routes to that department's skill, and a company's money to finance.

should_trigger.q: found a company for my new idea
start a new venture for me
we have an idea for X, help me stand it up
set our strategy for next year
refresh the OKRs for this quarter
what is our north star metric
should we enter the enterprise market
should I launch the product now or wait
which of these two vendors should we commit to for the next three years
go or no-go on the acquisition
should we sign an exclusive deal with this supplier
launch the new product across sales, legal and support
get the company ready for the seed round
execute the plan we agreed for next quarter across the departments

near_miss.q: brainstorm ways to grow the audience
what are my options for monetizing this
research the market size for this product
what is a weighted decision matrix
build me a skill that runs companies
write a standalone blog post
near_miss.route: editorial (board may dispatch it inside operate, but a lone post is editorial)

near_miss.q: make a chart of our revenue
should I refinance my mortgage
should I pay off my car loan or invest the money
draft an NDA with our supplier
close the books for October
build the financial model for the venture
near_miss.route: finance (a company's money; board convenes it only inside a company-wide run)

near_miss.q: draft the brand guide
write the onboarding SOP for our warehouse team
set up compensation bands for the engineering team
review our cloud access controls
define how we calculate churn
write the test strategy for our next release
build the customer onboarding playbook
write the press release announcing our funding round
